result.title: Ontology-guided multi-agent reasoning for explainable differential diagnosis
result.summary: Effective differential diagnosis depends on well structured and unambiguous patient case descriptions, since incomplete or ambiguous clinical information readily leads to diagnostic errors and inconsistent reasoning. Large Language Models (LLMs) have recently shown promising capabilities in medical question answering and clinical reasoning; however, even when achieving competitive performance on medical benchmarks, they often rely on pattern recognition learned from training data rather than grounded clinical evidence, and can generate plausible yet unsupported diagnostic conclusions. Their reasoning remains largely opaque, making it difficult for clinicians to assess the evidence and rationale behind a given recommendation. To address this gap, we propose an ontology-guided, multiagent differential diagnosis framework that replicates the iterative reasoning process of physicians. The framework grounds diagnostic inference in a structured, expert-curated medical knowledge base, enabling interpretation of symptoms, clinical findings, or disease relationships, while decomposing diagnosis into explicit, auditable reasoning steps. This ontology-based grounding constrains inference to evidence-backed associations, reducing hallucination and improving diagnostic transparency, traceability, and consistency. The system then identifies the most discriminative missing symptoms and generates targeted follow-up questions to reduce uncertainty through a process that mirrors to clinical inquiry. Together, these components improve the reliability, explainability, and diagnostic accuracy of AI-assisted differential diagnosis. The source code is publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 提出本体引导的多智能体鉴别诊断框架，把诊断推理约束在专家维护的医学知识库上，拆分为可审计的显式步骤，并主动挑选最具鉴别力的缺失症状生成追问以降低不确定性。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按信息增益选择下一步证据并追问」的机制，可能为 LVR 中 LOOK/STOP 的证据筛选与停止决策提供问题表述上的启发，可供核查；但该工作限于纯文本医学诊断，未涉及视觉状态或 latent 表示。
